title: loop-admin-runner-v1 launch request
description: Machine-readable contract for the launch request of the shared loop-admin runner protocol (spec/loop-admin-runner-v1.md). The root is the LaunchRequest; $defs carries the adapter-side shapes (observation, result, capabilities, usage). The contract is DESCRIPTIVE of shape: required fields, field types and closed value sets. It deliberately does NOT encode the cross-field rules the runner module enforces at start (standing-desk mode requires a desk binding and no workflow reference, workflow-stage mode requires work, node and attempt references and no desk binding, a resume session must be pinned to the request's role and profile, a mandatory requirement the adapter does not declare refuses the request, a budget carries at least one positive limit, credential-shaped content is refused at any depth of an extension, an object repeats no key); those need the whole request resolved, or are beyond what JSON Schema expresses. Where the two disagree the schema is the LOOSER of the two on purpose: every request the runner module accepts validates here, and keys match exactly, case included, with no null for a defined field. A usage figure that is absent is UNKNOWN, never zero.

version.description: The protocol version; exactly loop-admin-runner/v1. A consumer refuses any other value.

caller.description: The caller namespace. (caller, id) is the stable request identity.

desk.description: Standing-desk mode only: the desk binding.

work.description: Workflow-stage mode only: references to the existing canonical identities, never replacements for them.

packet.description: The role packet, by reference, with the trust of its source. It never carries credentials.

profile.description: The operator-approved pinned model, skill and tool profile. tools is the complete list the invocation may request; an empty list pins none. There is no fallback model field: a different model is refused, never substituted.

authority.description: The externally validated claim or ownership generation the launch runs under. The runner does not mint or validate it; validated_by names what did.

budget.description: A reference to the caller's budget reservation, with the scope the adapter must enforce. No limit may be negative and at least one must be positive.

resume.description: Optional session to resume, pinned to the request's role and profile. An adapter that does not declare resume refuses; a fresh session is never substituted.

require.description: Mandatory capabilities and extensions. A capability name (resume, cancel-ack, budget-launch, budget-request, telemetry, snapshot, launch-dedupe) or ext:<name>. A consumer that does not provide, or does not define, a listed name refuses the request.

ext.description: Optional extensions, ignored unless named in require as ext:<name>. Never a place for credentials: every value is decoded and walked, and a credential-shaped string or a key naming a credential slot, at any depth, refuses the request.

usage.description: Token and cost accounting. An absent field is unknown, never zero; a measured 0 is a real reading; a consumer treats a negative figure as unknown.

trust.description: Model output is untrusted until a caller's own check accepts it; an adapter cannot raise it.

note.description: The model's own text. It carries no authority.

result.description: The adapter's terminal report. caller and id echo the invocation identity, and generation the authority generation the attempt ran under; a result echoing another invocation is refused. It is NOT acceptance.

observation.description: One adapter report. finished, failed and stopped are absorbing: a later report leaving one, or a finished report with another result or model, is refused and recorded nowhere. A finished observation with no actual_model is not accepted: an unreported model is unknown, not the pinned one.

capabilities.description: What an adapter declares. The zero value declares nothing; every optional facility is opt-in.
